The kite on a quiet afternoon

My brother and I made a yellow kite on Friday. On Saturday, we took it to the park with Mum. I expected it to rise as soon as I held the string. Instead, it lay on the ____1____. I pulled harder, but nothing useful happened. My brother looked at the leaves above us. They were hardly ____2____. There was very little ____3____. The kite had not failed a test simply by staying ____4____. It needed conditions we had not ____5____.

Mum suggested waiting rather than running through a crowded part of the park. We sat at a clear place and watched other visitors. A boy nearby was drawing the trees. He asked if he could include our kite in his ____6____. I nearly said it was not ready because it had not flown. He said a kite could be interesting on the ground too. Its bright colour made a cheerful ____7____ against the grass. We placed it where he could see the shape and kept the string ____8____. Soon my brother began drawing beside him. Our afternoon had found another ____9____ while we waited for the weather to ____10____.

Later, a breeze moved the branches. Mum helped us find a suitable open space, and the kite finally rose. I watched its yellow wings against the blue ____11____. The boy showed us his finished drawing before leaving. It recorded a different part of the afternoon, one I had almost ____12____. At home, we put the picture beside the kite. The kite had done what we made it to do, but the waiting had not been ____13____. I still hoped for wind on our next visit. I simply knew that a plan could have room for something ____14____. Sometimes an enjoyable day begins with the thing you wanted, and sometimes it begins while you are waiting for it to ____15____.
